mapping_rule: When attention is scarce, expose low-cost cues that let the receiver estimate downstream value.
broken_features: a cue does not guarantee destination quality
example: A headline should provide enough scent to justify the next click without giving away or falsifying the content.

mapping_rule: Convert an unanswered but reachable question into a state difference that pulls the reader forward.
broken_features: not all conflict is curiosity
example: “Why did a good product fail?” creates a gap; expectation-vs-outcome creates tension.

mapping_rule: Resolve tension with progressively stronger evidence rather than rhetoric alone.
broken_features: evidence strength is not dramatic intensity
example: Use case, independent data, and reproducible observation to settle a surprising claim.

mapping_rule: Treat observed independent behavior as one rung of evidence, not universal proof.
broken_features: popularity can be wrong or manipulated
example: Repeat purchase is stronger than likes but weaker than controlled evidence for causal claims.

mapping_rule: Place authority evidence at a rung appropriate to domain expertise and independence.
broken_features: authority outside scope does not transfer
example: A cardiologist is relevant to cardiac evidence, not automatically to software architecture.

mapping_rule: Compress recurring structures into named modules with stable interfaces, then expand them in context.
broken_features: a semantic pattern is not always an executable module
example: Turn a repeated content structure into a reusable template with configurable slots.

mapping_rule: Compress a target audience’s recurring relation pattern, then expand it into modality-specific expressions.
broken_features: emotional response differs across modalities
example: The same “loss of control” structure can appear in headline, image composition, voice cadence, and story.

mapping_rule: User outcomes can feed adoption, and adoption can change value, creating coupled loops.
broken_features: network effects require participant-dependent value
example: Better community answers attract members; more members create more answers.

mapping_rule: Feedback is one maintenance mechanism that counteracts drift and decay.
broken_features: feedback alone cannot supply all maintenance energy
example: A knowledge base needs usage feedback plus editorial cleanup.

mapping_rule: Represent a threshold crossing as the trigger for a discrete state transition.
broken_features: some transitions are probabilistic, not deterministic
example: Lead score > threshold may move a prospect into human review.

mapping_rule: Historical choices can reshape the landscape so trajectories repeatedly return to a familiar region.
broken_features: attractors can exist without historical lock-in
example: A team’s early tool choices create routines that pull future work back to the same stack.

mapping_rule: When early choices create lock-in, preserve reversible options longer.
broken_features: too much optionality can prevent commitment
example: Use an adapter layer before locking the whole product to one vendor.

mapping_rule: Independent backups preserve future action after failure.
broken_features: redundancy duplicates capability; options may be non-duplicate alternatives
example: Keep two independent distribution channels rather than one platform.

mapping_rule: Modular boundaries make redundant replacement paths practical.
broken_features: modularity does not automatically create redundancy
example: Two interchangeable provider adapters can back each other up.

mapping_rule: Clear module boundaries localize drift and reduce maintenance propagation.
broken_features: bad module boundaries create more entropy
example: Version each workflow module and test its interface separately.

mapping_rule: Filtering increases the share of scarce attention spent on decision-relevant signals.
broken_features: aggressive filtering can delete weak but important signals
example: Daily intelligence brief removes duplicated low-value reports.

mapping_rule: Repeated audience/platform reward changes which messages survive and therefore which resonant forms become common.
broken_features: resonance is psychological fit; selection is population change
example: Content variants aligned with a niche’s identity are disproportionately retained and repeated.

mapping_rule: Repeated selection can lock a population/system into locally successful strategies.
broken_features: selection can also drive continual change
example: A platform rewards one content style until creators specialize around it.

mapping_rule: Exploration buys information and preserves strategic options; exploitation harvests known value.
broken_features: option value does not specify experimentation budget
example: Reserve some content slots for new audience hypotheses.

mapping_rule: Use feedback from experiments to shift resources toward or away from exploitation.
broken_features: noisy feedback can cause overreaction
example: Weekly results update next week’s explore/exploit mix.

mapping_rule: Inverse inference should enumerate candidate causes and climb evidence rungs to discriminate among them.
broken_features: evidence may still leave multiple solutions
example: Reverse-engineer a viral post, then test candidate mechanisms across more posts.

mapping_rule: A proposed hidden mechanism is credible only inside conditions where it continues to predict observations.
broken_features: some boundaries are unknown initially
example: A hook structure may work on short video but fail in long-form professional writing.

mapping_rule: Local cues plus uneven friction determine which path is most likely to be followed.
broken_features: humans can choose costly paths for identity or values
example: Simplify the high-value CTA and make its benefit legible.

mapping_rule: Constraints shape transition probabilities between states.
broken_features: state machines can be deterministic
example: Payment friction lowers probability of prospect->customer transition.

mapping_rule: Define evidence requirements for moving an object/claim to a stronger state.
broken_features: not all evidence systems are state machines
example: Mark a mapping seed->tested->validated only after repeatable evaluation.

mapping_rule: Identity resonance can increase the weight assigned to peer behavior from the same perceived group.
broken_features: resonance can exist without observing peers
example: A founder trusts a case study more when it comes from a similar business.

mapping_rule: Evidence supports claims only within the scope actually tested.
broken_features: strong theory may generalize beyond a sample but still needs justification
example: One platform case should not be presented as universal social-media law.

mapping_rule: A compressed pattern must carry its validity conditions when expanded elsewhere.
broken_features: some expansions intentionally explore beyond known bounds
example: A “feedback loop” template must specify delay, signal quality, and controllability in the target domain.

mapping_rule: Network effects may become visible only after participation/connectivity crosses a critical level.
broken_features: many network effects are gradual
example: A marketplace can feel empty until enough supply and demand coexist.

mapping_rule: Larger networks gain value but also produce moderation, coordination, and quality-maintenance costs.
broken_features: not every network has strong maintenance burden
example: A growing community requires stronger governance to prevent signal collapse.

mapping_rule: Stable interfaces preserve the ability to swap future implementations.
broken_features: interface stability may constrain innovation
example: Wrap an embedding provider behind an adapter.

mapping_rule: Compression can fit more decision-relevant structure into scarce attention.
broken_features: compression can oversimplify
example: Lead with one compressed idea, then allow deeper expansion.

mapping_rule: Noise makes hidden-cause inference ill-posed; aggregate and discriminate before attributing cause.
broken_features: some inverse problems are deterministic with clean data
example: Do not infer content strategy from one anomalous post.

mapping_rule: Use cheap cues to prioritize which uncertain paths deserve exploration budget.
broken_features: cues can be deceptive
example: Scan titles/abstracts before deep-reading every paper.

mapping_rule: Feedback gain can push a system across a threshold into a new regime.
broken_features: threshold may come from external shock instead
example: Referral growth can become self-sustaining after a minimum active base.

mapping_rule: Maintenance interventions can reshape or escape undesirable attractors.
broken_features: not all attractors are undesirable or controllable
example: Regular moderation prevents a community from converging to low-signal norms.

mapping_rule: Selection rewards exploitation of current fitness while environmental change creates value for exploration.
broken_features: biological populations do not consciously budget exploration
example: A creator repeats winning formats but tests new ones before platform preferences shift.

mapping_rule: Authority and peer behavior are distinct trust channels that can reinforce or contradict each other.
broken_features: mechanisms of credibility differ
example: Expert endorsement plus independent user adoption is stronger than either alone for many purchase decisions.

mapping_rule: A cue can reveal the existence and size of a useful knowledge gap.
broken_features: too little scent creates no perceived gap
example: “The expensive mistake happens after deployment, not before” signals a specific unresolved gap.

mapping_rule: Cues that match an existing identity/problem have higher perceived path value.
broken_features: resonance may bias people toward low-quality information
example: Use the target group’s real vocabulary, then substantiate it.
